title: fix(devx): readDeclaredTypeSurface returns the declared member surface for interface/class/enum and the whole RHS of a multi-line alias
body:
Fixes #15489

`readDeclaredTypeSurface` is predicate 4's reader — the one thing paying for
`type-surface-only`'s exemption from the `no-migration-prescription` refusal. It returned
two readings that could not carry the comparison it is asked to make.

## Misread 1 — an `interface` / `class` / `enum` read back as its own NAME

The branch returned `type: symbol`. A symbol's name is the one part of a declaration that a
member removal cannot change, so predicate 4's before/after reading of an interface was
constant across every diff, and the refusal at the founding-case site printed that constant
to the author.

Measured on the card's real specimen, `packages/rest/src/export-format.ts#ExportFieldMeta`
across `9b9b70f80` (which retired eight of its keys). Member types are elided below to keep
angle-bracket-shaped fragments out of this body; the counts and the `erased` values are the
reader's own output.

| rev | before this PR | after this PR |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `9b9b70f80^` | `type` = `ExportFieldMeta` | member surface, **15 members**, 329 chars |
| `9b9b70f80` | `type` = `ExportFieldMeta` | member surface, **7 members**, 181 chars |
| verdict | identical — the reading says "unchanged" | **differs — eight members fewer** |

Member names at base: `name`, `type?`, `label?`, `options?`, `reference?`, `displayField?`,
`multiple?`, `required?`, `system?`, `readonly?`, `hasDefault?`, `min?`, `max?`,
`minLength?`, `maxLength?`. At head the last eight are gone.

The card's three-member `ActorUser` specimen, verbatim:

```
before:  type = "ActorUser"
after:   type = "{ id: string; roles: string[]; positions: string[]; }"
```

## Misread 2 — an alias RHS truncated at the first `;` ANYWHERE

The RHS was read with a lazy `[\s\S]*?` up to the first semicolon in the remaining file
text. That semicolon is the one ending the alias's **first member**, so every multi-line
object alias was truncated; a semicolon inside a string literal truncated harder still; and
an alias carrying no semicolon at all over-read into the next statement.

```
export type Row = {          before:  "{ a: string"
  a: string;                 after:   "{ a: string; b: number; }"
  b: number;
};

export type Sep = ';' | ',';  before:  "'"
                              after:   "';' | ','"
```

The replacement walks the RHS to the first `;` at nesting depth **zero**, brace/bracket/paren
balanced and string-aware (structure is walked on the comment- and literal-masked projection;
the answer is sliced out of the comment-masked one, so a literal's own text survives while its
brackets never steer the walk). A generic alias keeps its whole RHS, and a type-parameter list
carrying a default is skipped by bracket matching rather than by the old
"angle-bracket-with-no-equals" regex that could not see past it. With no semicolon at all, the
alias ends at the end of the **declaration** — a depth-0 newline whose next non-blank line
opens a new top-level statement — not at the end of the file.

Angle brackets are deliberately **not** counted in that walk: a fat-arrow function type ends
in one, so counting them makes every function type close a depth nothing opened. Nothing is
lost — a `;` cannot reach depth 0 inside type arguments without passing through a brace,
bracket or paren first.

## `.erased` does not move — the invariance control

`.erased` is the one field both misreads left alone (an interface is concrete whatever its
body says, and a truncated RHS is concrete for the same reason the whole one is), which is
exactly why the existing battery asserted `.erased` and stayed green through both defects.
So it is also the field this PR must not disturb. Every reading was taken before and after
the change, on the same tree:

```
ActorUser (3-member interface)      erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME
TSO-U17 alias any                   erased True  -> True    shape-same=True  SAME
TSO-U18 alias object                erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME
TSO-U19 missing symbol              erased None  -> None    shape-same=True  SAME
multi-line object alias             erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME
alias with a `;` in a string        erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME
generic alias                       erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME
class                               erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME
enum                                erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME
ExportFieldMeta @ 9b9b70f80^        erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME
ExportFieldMeta @ 9b9b70f80         erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME
real ActorUser @ HEAD               erased False -> False   shape-same=True  SAME

ERASED+SHAPE INVARIANCE: HOLDS
```

The `interface` / `class` / `enum` branch cannot move it structurally either: `erased` is
`false` by construction there, so no reading of the body reaches it.

## The refusal message

Predicate 4's already-CONCRETE refusal now prints the real surface. A whole interface body
is long — the specimen is 329 chars — so `printableSurface` truncates **explicitly**: the
first 160 characters, an ellipsis, then the member count and the full length in parentheses,
so an author can tell "long" from "all of it". A short surface is printed byte-identical. The
member count is separator-counted at depth 0 and says so in its own docblock; it is a figure
for a notice, not a contract. A declaration whose body cannot be read at all prints "its
declared surface is not readable here" rather than a bare null.

## Self-test

The battery asserted only `.erased` on these readings (`TSO-U16`–`TSO-U19`). Eleven `.type`
cases were added (`TSO-U20`–`TSO-U30`) plus `TSO-6048d`, which holds the **real** `ActorUser`
in this tree to a brace body naming `positions` rather than to the string `ActorUser`. Both
battery floors were raised with them (`TSO-U` 19 to 30, `TSO-6048` 7 to 8). No case was
weakened.

```
before:  292 assertions over real temp git repos (real scan()/assertInputs() path)
after:   304 assertions over real temp git repos (real scan()/assertInputs() path)
```

## Verification

Exit codes captured **before** any pipe (`cmd > file 2>&1; EXIT=$?`); verdict lines are the
gates' own.

| command | exit | verdict line |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --self-test` | 0 | `check-adr-0087-registration --self-test: 304 assertions over real temp git repos (real scan()/assertInputs() path)` |
| `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` | 0 | `check-adr-0087-registration: this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset (0 non-breaking changeset(s) seen).` |
| `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` | 0 | `dispatch-gates self-test: 1445 cases pass.` |
| `pnpm check:nul-bytes` | 0 | `check-nul-bytes: OK (scanned 7565 text file(s) ... no raw ASCII control bytes).` |
| `node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` | 0 | `comment-mask corpus sweep: 5960 files, 0 disagree, 0 unparseable` |
| `node scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` | 0 | green — this file is ADR-anchored |
| the other 27 commands `dispatch-gates --changed --commands` emitted | 0 | all green; the full list is in the report on #15489 |

### Ablation, per misread

Trap-guarded (`trap restore EXIT INT TERM`, absolute paths seeded from
`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), the fix committed first, the mutation proved on disk by
before/after occurrence counts of both the removed and the injected text, and each restore
proved by `git hash-object` equality against the HEAD blob plus an empty `git diff HEAD`.
No rebuild leg applies: this gate is a plain `.mjs` run directly by node, with no `dist/`
between the source and the run.

```
=== ABLATION: misread (1): interface/class/enum returns the SYMBOL NAME again ===
  on-disk proof: removed-text count 1 -> 0 ; injected-text count 0 -> 1
  self-test EXIT=1 (expected non-zero)
  - TSO-6048d ... (got type: "ActorUser").
  - TSO-U20: an exported interface reads as its declared MEMBER SURFACE ...
  - TSO-U21: a `class` body is read the same way, nested braces included
  - TSO-U22: an `enum` body is read the same way
  restored: blob == HEAD

=== ABLATION: misread (2): the alias RHS reverts to the lazy first-semicolon regex ===
  on-disk proof: removed-text count 1 -> 0 ; injected-text count 0 -> 1
  self-test EXIT=1 (expected non-zero)
  - TSO-U23: a MULTI-LINE object alias survives the `;` that ends its FIRST member ...
  - TSO-U24: a `;` INSIDE a string literal does not terminate the RHS ...
  - TSO-U25: a GENERIC alias keeps its whole RHS ...
  - TSO-U26: an alias with NO `;` ends at the END OF THE DECLARATION ...
  restored: blob == HEAD

ABLATION COMPLETE
  restore: blob 01a653279181d038126eeef16287ee7365211dfa == HEAD, git diff HEAD empty
```

### What is NOT measured

- The 11 gate families that apply once a changeset exists. This PR touches `scripts/**` only
  and publishes nothing, so it carries no changeset and is labelled `skip-changeset`; those
  families are derived against a path that does not exist. `check:empty-changeset` and
  `check:objectui-changeset` were run and are green.
- The 3 families whose argv takes a value from the workflow (`RUNNER_TEMP`, a shard matrix
  index) — they have no value outside a CI run.
- Nothing. The whole-repo `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) was run rather than
  narrowed: exit 0.

## Scope

One file: `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`. `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` is
untouched — `maskCommentsAndLiterals` was already in this file and already used by
`memberReturnAnnotation`, predicate 4's sibling reader. The step-4 reference scan of
`runtime-interface-only` still reads `maskComments` alone, so the literals-are-not-masked
posture the ADR anchor guards is unchanged; no diff line touches it.
